Private Jerome and Prescott Tour from Phoenix and Scottsdale

Scottsdale Sprinters runs a private Jerome and Prescott tour from Phoenix and Scottsdale as one vehicle and one chauffeur held for a 10-hour day: the group is driven to the Jerome stops it has confirmed, on to Prescott if that leg is part of the approved route, and home again. The second town is conditional in the row itself, so this page quotes the tour's own itinerary — "Continue to Prescott if included in the approved route" — and builds everything around the stops your group actually confirms. The published window is 8-10 hours and it bills 9 hours, so the day starts at $1,125 and the 14-seat Executive Black Sprinter is $1,305 before 8% tax. Reservations: (623) 986-6339.

Last updated: September 18, 2026

Can you visit Jerome and Prescott in one day from Phoenix?

Yes, and this tour is the version that admits what that costs. It publishes 9 steps across a 8-10 hours window, and the sixth of them makes the second town conditional rather than automatic: "Continue to Prescott if included in the approved route". Both towns fit; what decides it is your own confirmed list. Read that step as the honest version of a day-trip promise. A single vehicle held for 10 requested hours can cover a hillside town and a courthouse square inside one window — but only if the stops in between are chosen rather than assumed. The row asks for the choosing up front: "Choose the exact Jerome attraction, Prescott endpoint, and desired time at each stop before requesting transportation. Arizona State Parks publishes current Jerome State Historic Park details, the City of Prescott publishes downtown parking information, and current road conditions should be rechecked before the trip. A specific curb, parking space, or attraction entry is not guaranteed by the transportation request." That is also why nothing on this page prints a schedule with times against it. The vehicle is yours for the window; where the hours go is a decision your group makes with the reservations team in writing.

What is a private Jerome and Prescott tour from Phoenix and Scottsdale?

It is the whole vehicle and one chauffeur held for a 10-hour day up the mountain and back, not a seat on somebody else's coach. A range of vehicles is offered for it, from 6 to 29 seats, and priced from $1,125 to $2,655, every figure quoted in writing first. Scottsdale Sprinters sells the transport around the stops you confirm, never the attractions themselves. Your group decides who is aboard and how the hours are spent; the chauffeur drives, parks, waits while you are in a museum or on a gallery street, and drives home — which on a day with a winding mountain leg is most of the point. Per head the arithmetic is plainer than it looks. The 14-seat Executive Black Sprinter splits $1,305 across its seats, about $93 each; the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) splits $2,025 across 29, about $70. Those are the current published hourly rates carried across this day, never a fare per person, and admissions are separate.

How does the day run, from the first Jerome stop to the return?

The tour publishes 9 steps and states the day as 8-10 hours. Two of them are explicitly yours to fix before anything is confirmed — the first Jerome stop and the lunch stop — and one, the Prescott leg, only happens if your approved route includes it. "Drive to the first confirmed Jerome stop" is the step everything else hangs off: it is what "Morning pickup" is set backward from. "Lunch at a confirmed Jerome venue" is worded the same way on purpose — the venue is your booking, not ours, and the vehicle is already paid for while you are in it. The row also publishes what the day is meant to show: Jerome ghost town, Jerome State Historic Park, Prescott Courthouse Square, Whiskey Row saloons, Art galleries, Mountain views. That list is the whole brief, and the last two steps before the drive home — "Courthouse Square exploration" and "Whiskey Row historic saloons" — are the Prescott half of it.

Which vehicle fits the group, and what does the day cost?

Group size decides it. This tour offers a range of vehicles, and every row below prices the identical 10-hour day: the published hourly rate times 9 billable hours, because 10 requested hours earn 1 free hour on the standard ladder, against each vehicle's own 4-hour minimum. Up to 6 travellers the Luxury SUV (Suburban) runs the day for $1,125, which is where the row's own list starts with the Luxury SUV (Suburban); the Executive Black Sprinter and Executive White Sprinter share a rate at $145 an hour. Past 14 seats it is the Mini Bus (24 Pax) and the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax). The per-seat column divides the day total by seated capacity — friends splitting one fare. The Luxury SUV (Suburban) is the least expensive day at $1,125; the Mini Bus (24 Pax) the least expensive seat at $69. A hillside town with narrow streets is also a reason some groups take the smaller unit and pay more per seat. What is in the fare, and what is not?

A 10-hour day in the 14-seat Executive Black Sprinter is $1,305 before 8% tax — $145 an hour across 9 billable hours, roughly $93 a seat split 14 ways. The least expensive vehicle on the list runs the same day for $1,125. Three rules build every number: the day is priced by the hour against each vehicle's published minimum, hours above the ladder's rungs earn free hours, and 8% tax is the only addition. Nothing is by the mile or per passenger. 50% is taken today by card. What the fare excludes is the part of the day that is not ours to sell — museum admission, a tour someone else runs, a table at the lunch stop. Lunch is a stop rather than a service for the same reason: "No eating or food inside the vehicle. Drinks are fine; snacks wait for the next stop."

How far is Prescott, and what decides the route up the mountain?

One distance, and it is this site's own. The published 86301 area guide answers it in a single sentence — "Prescott is approximately 100 miles north of Phoenix via I-17 and Highway 69" — and this page adds nothing to it. What the route looks like on the day is a written decision, not a number we publish here. The row is deliberate about that: "Mountain access depends on current weather, closures, and vehicle restrictions. The team reviews the requested route and current road information before written confirmation." The vehicle restrictions the row names are a real constraint on which unit can be sent, which is one more reason the group-size conversation happens before the quote and not after it. No drive time appears anywhere on this page, in either direction: the vehicle is held for the window you book, and the chauffeur drives it.

What is there to see in Jerome, and what is on Courthouse Square?

The row names 6 things and the state park describes itself. Arizona State Parks writes of the historic park that "This former home is now a museum devoted to the history of the Jerome area and the Douglas family." That museum is step 3 of the published itinerary; the galleries and shops are step 4. The park adds the detail that decides how long a group lingers: "There are more displays outside along with a picnic area offering a beautiful panoramic view of the Verde Valley." Bags, coats and anything bought in the galleries go back to the vehicle between stops rather than around the town with you. On the Prescott half, the row answers the question visitors actually ask: "Whiskey Row is a historic Prescott district near Courthouse Plaza. Check current visitor information, venue hours, age policies, and any reservations directly before adding a stop to the route." Scottsdale Sprinters books no venue for you, and the linked City of Prescott page is where downtown parking information is published — the row says so itself.

Where can the day start, and how is it quoted?

Pickup is a street address in any of the 10 metro cities with a published service-area page, not a zone or a depot. Reserving takes 3 things — the date, the number of people and one address — plus the Jerome stop and the Prescott decision as soon as you have them. The published service areas are Scottsdale, Phoenix, Paradise Valley, Tempe, Mesa, Chandler, Gilbert, Glendale, Cave Creek and San Tan Valley. One pickup address for the whole party keeps a group together, and the ride back is the half of a mountain day nobody should be driving. Every figure here is today's published table; the quote you act on is the written one, naming the vehicle, the hours, the 8% tax and the 50% deposit, confirmed before anything is charged. Call Scottsdale Sprinters on (623) 986-6339, or send those 3 things and request a current quote.
